newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO'S FOX KNOCKS STATE CONTROL OF PEMEX.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO'S FOX KNOCKS STATE CONTROL OF PEMEX.

text.p: Vicente Fox, a Mexican governor who says he will run for the presidency as an opposition candidate in 2000, on Wednesday criticized the state control of oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).

"The company has failed in contributing to Mexicans the wealth and profits that we are expecting," the Guanajuato governor from the conservative National Action Party (PAN) told Reuters Financial Television in a live interview.
He said Mexico's natural resources were sacred and should be kept for Mexicans, but the company was poorly managed.
"The administration, the processing, the selling, the distribution -- that should be done much better than its been up to now," he said.
In the past Fox has supported further privatization of Pemex -- a risky admission in a country where the oil company is considered by many as much a symbol of national pride as the flag.
Mexico recently allowed limited foreign investment in other previously-taboo areas such as electricity generation and natural gas distribution.

But political parties -- especially the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party -- have been reluctant to go further, and every year Mexicans remember with pride the date in 1938 when the country expropriated its oil and kicked out foreign oil companies.
